title: the machine that takes only QR

opening.dialogue: A life is a sending, and tonight the sending has stalled at the change machine: the auntie's cash is folded in a handkerchief, the screen wants a code she cannot make, and the queue behind her is learning its own patience. Note sits on his charging-corner stool with the laundry basket at his feet, a boy with no power-saving mode, watching the machine the way a doctor watches a fever.

I can make it take her money. I just need the machine to believe she's her. He taps the laminated score report on the counter, then the word notebook. Write it down for me — what the app says when it fails. I'll read it back to the machine.

turns.speaker: char_note
stage_directions: He lifts the laundry basket onto his knees and squints at the auntie's phone, thumb hovering over the queue of names in her app.
turns.dialogue: Her grandson's the one who tops her up. He's probably not coming tonight — the app's already guessing it. See how it greys out his name?

turns.speaker: char_note
stage_directions: He slides the word notebook across the counter and presses a pen into Lek's hand, then points at the error screen on the auntie's phone.
turns.dialogue: Write exactly what the screen says. Not what it means — what it says. The machine only trusts the letters it printed.

turns.speaker: char_note
stage_directions: He stands on the stool's rung and holds the orange queue vest up to the light, checking the camp worker's name tag against the auntie's app photo.
turns.dialogue: Everything's under control — the queue just doesn't know it yet. The camp worker goes first, then the airport woman, then her. That's the order the machine will accept.

turns.speaker: char_note
stage_directions: He sets the circle envelope on the counter beside the mattress ad printout and rubs his eyes with the heel of his hand.
turns.dialogue: You look run down, phi. Sit. The machine and I have an understanding — it takes my word for things, and I take its word for things. We're both tired of the other.

turns.speaker: char_note
stage_directions: He turns the permit photo over and traces the camp's address with one finger, then holds it up beside the auntie's app profile.
turns.dialogue: The app wants a province. She's from here, but the machine only knows the province on the photo. Which province is on the photo, phi?

turns.speaker: char_note
stage_directions: He holds the laminated score report up to the ring light and taps the score line, then sets it down beside the stamp-drawer keys.
turns.dialogue: There's a high chance the machine takes the score instead of the app. It's the only paper in the soi with a number the machine already believes.

turns.speaker: char_note
stage_directions: He glances sideways at the airport woman's phone screen, then back at the auntie's, and taps the two profiles side by side on the counter.
turns.dialogue: She's still single on the app — no family account linked. That's the problem. The machine wants a second name on her, and she's only ever had her own.

turns.speaker: char_note
stage_directions: He holds up the orange queue vest in one hand and the auntie's handkerchief in the other, then lays both across the laundry basket's rim.
turns.dialogue: Which kind does the machine like — the vest with the name tag, or the handkerchief with the cash? One it reads, one it counts. Pick.

note_turn_1.speaker: char_note
note_turn_1.line: He names the grandson as a no-show and shows Lek how the app greys out the missing name — the machine has already decided she is alone tonight.

note_turn_2.speaker: char_note
note_turn_2.line: Lek writes the error text into the word notebook, and Note reads it back to the machine in the flat voice the screen trusts.

note_turn_3.speaker: char_note
note_turn_3.line: He reorders the queue by name tag and app photo: camp worker, airport woman, then the auntie — and the machine's screen stops blinking at her.

note_turn_4.speaker: char_note
note_turn_4.line: He sets the circle envelope on the counter, its flap already loose, and admits the machine and he are both tired of being the only ones who know.

note_turn_5.speaker: char_note
note_turn_5.line: Note reads the camp's province off the permit photo and types it into the auntie's app — the profile accepts it, and the error screen changes color.

note_turn_6.speaker: char_note
note_turn_6.line: He holds the score report to the light and bets the machine will take a printed number over a spoken name — the screen flickers, considering.

note_turn_7.speaker: char_note
note_turn_7.line: Note points out the auntie has no linked family account, which is why the machine keeps asking her to prove she is herself.

note_turn_8.speaker: char_note
note_turn_8.line: He lays the vest and the handkerchief on the basket rim and waits for Lek to choose which one the machine will read as proof.

finale.dialogue: He takes the stamp-drawer keys from Lek's hand and turns them once in the lock, then hands back the basket, dry and folded. The machine takes only QR, but tonight it took her word for it.
The auntie carries her basket home herself, and the queue behind her closes like water. Note goes back to his stool, a boy with no power-saving mode, already helping the next phone.

obj_word_notebook.name: the word notebook
obj_word_notebook.description: Cardboard cover, spine split at the third signature, every page a stranger's word copied in Lek's hand — the ones nobody paid for.

obj_score_report.name: the laminated score report
obj_score_report.description: Exam result folded into a plastic sleeve, the score line worn pale from being read at the counter — three points short, twice.

obj_stamp_keys.name: the stamp-drawer keys
obj_stamp_keys.description: Three brass keys on a wire ring, one bent from the year the drawer jammed, warm from Lek's pocket.

obj_mattress_ad.name: the mattress ad printout
obj_mattress_ad.description: A4 sheet, toner still tacky at the edge, a sale price printed twice because the first run smudged.

obj_permit_photo.name: the permit photo
obj_permit_photo.description: Passport photo stapled to a construction permit, the camp's province written in a hand that pressed too hard.

obj_ring_light.name: the ring light
obj_ring_light.description: Clip-on circle light, one segment dead, borrowed from Je Fah's back room and never returned.

obj_laundry_basket.name: the laundry basket
obj_laundry_basket.description: Plastic basket, handle cracked and taped, a full load of the auntie's washing sitting damp in it since the machine refused her.

obj_vest_orange.name: the orange queue vest
obj_vest_orange.description: High-visibility vest with a camp name tag pinned crooked, the reflective strip gone grey at the fold.

obj_share_envelope.name: the circle envelope
obj_share_envelope.description: Brown envelope, flap loose, a payout counted twice and a note in pencil about someone two weeks late.
